target_customer: Small e-commerce and social commerce merchants in Nigeria selling through their own channels, who pay for delivery and fulfillment
problem: Small online merchants in Nigeria struggle with unreliable local delivery and costly international shipping and fulfillment.
business_model: Per-shipment fees on local and international delivery and fulfillment, plus payments
product_category: Logistics and fulfillment for social commerce

founders.name: Emotu Balogun
previous_startups: Fashion marketplace for Nigerian merchants (outcome not stated on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists 10+ years in software and product development.

competitors.name: GIG Logistics (GIGL)
competitors.what: Nigerian courier and delivery company with the GIGGO app launched 2019

competitors.name: Topship
competitors.what: Shipping infrastructure platform for African businesses

technical_complexity.rationale: Software to aggregate couriers, fulfillment centers and international shipping with payments; operations heavy in a hard market.

defensibility.rationale: Merchant integrations and carrier rates help, but couriers and other delivery apps could offer the same service.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found; the company expanded into Ghana and later reported 7,500 merchants on the YC page.

market_need_then: Nigerian social commerce was growing and merchants lacked reliable delivery; Sendbox reported over 10,000 vendors and 200,000 deliveries at its Oct 2021 seed.

identity.voice_and_tone: Described as a social commerce app for deliveries, payments and online shopping

brand_strength.rationale: Clear name matching the send and box delivery idea, covered widely by African tech press, but no evidence of brand assets or community.

outcome_analysis: Sendbox raised a $1.8M seed in October 2021 after YC and reported thousands of merchants, then stayed active with a team of 25 but no later round was found. It rides Nigerian social commerce growth, though logistics margins and local competitors limit the upside; the distribution factor is an inference from traction claims.
notes: Seed reported by TechCrunch, TechCabal, Disrupt Africa and others (not opened, seen in search results). An earlier pre-seed is mentioned in coverage (total about $2M) without amount, so coverage is partial. Founding year differs: YC says 2018, press says building began in 2016 and launch two years later. Competitor evidence comes from CB Insights and a directory with unknown dates; GIGGO launch 2019 is from a search summary. Kwik, Lori and Sendstack were searched but not confirmed. Brand name origin not found.
